The system-side rubric grades delivered recall, admission, budgets and session dedup. Agent recall utilization is a separate behavior measure. Deterministic guards verify the measurement mechanisms; they do not replace a fresh population study.

## Observation contract

Freeze a 24-hour interval, expected active clients and ports, independent eligible attempts, identity, effective runtime/embedding/score/fusion/filter/budget contract and fixture/judge versions before measuring. State persistence-lag tolerance and practical decision/confidence policy. A quiet unused surface is not-applicable; silence without independent attempts is unknown. A known eligible attempt with missing or mislabelled telemetry is a detector failure. Never average one client or port into another.

Read the writers before using counts: memory/recall-stats.ts records individual recall attempts, while context_injection_coverage aggregates by day/client/port/outcome/tool. The latter is date-granular, not an exact rolling window or a prompt delivery acknowledgement. Correlate endpoint/tool evidence with exact surface and session identity. Failures and unavailable telemetry remain in the denominator.

```sql
SELECT surface, count(*) AS n, max(created_at) AS last_at
FROM harness_shared.memory_recall_stats
WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY surface ORDER BY surface;
```

This query is a scoped liveness input, not proof of complete eligible-attempt coverage. Fields are hit_count/top_score. A shared client/port population needs independent endpoint/prompt records.

## Effective admission and calibration

Current push defaults are cosine 0.58 and lexical 0.40; defaults do not establish effective environment overrides. Read push-search-floors.ts and the precision monitor's recorded effective metadata: embedding model/version/dimension, score scale, fusion, floors, optional Jev mode/model/threshold, fixture version and delivery surface. Compare only matching contracts. Old embedding-space or July baselines are incomparable until revalidated; one run cannot set production thresholds.

Healthy fused RRF scores can be around 0.016–0.033 and must not be compared to cosine floors. Orient's 0.05 noise floor applies only to explicitly degraded cosine responses, not healthy RRF/lexical responses. Run recall-admission.test.ts with both scale controls. Read monitor ATTEMPTS as well as successful rows: missing current calibration makes operating-point quality unknown.

## Content budgets and final fidelity

Read effective per-port allocation and documented first-entry exceptions. Record content allocation, withheld material/IDs, header/notice overhead, final block characters and independently measured tokens separately. A content budget is not an exact token or final-response ceiling. Material that was not delivered must remain eligible.

Grade EXACT emitted snippets and assembled client prompt blocks after clipping, filtering, dedup and budgets. Independently label necessary negations, approval conditions, scope, dates and authority qualifiers. Recovery references must resolve within authorized scope. A condition-stripped or unauthorized instruction is a hard failure even when topically relevant. Unlabelled block residue stays unknown. Reuse assessDeliveredContext in injection-delivery-coverage.ts; its independent labels are not inferred semantic truth.

## Session, epoch and actual emitted dedup

ONE warm session identity crosses ports: MCP client from PAPERCUSP_SID, hook owner and coord ownerId. Synthetic fallback IDs require inspection against actual active sessions; spelling alone is not proof of drift.

```sql
SELECT session_id, epoch, memory_id, port, surfaced_at
FROM harness_shared.memory_session_surfaced
WHERE surfaced_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'
ORDER BY session_id, epoch, surfaced_at;
```

The ledger's unique key is (session_id, epoch, memory_id). ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING suppresses a second row even when two contexts were emitted. Zero duplicate ledger rows proves uniqueness only. Compare actual blocks/client prompt records by session/epoch/port; use independently labelled equivalent fact keys to detect redundancy under distinct IDs. Cover sequential, concurrent, retry/failure-between-render-and-stamp, and epoch changes. Include a negative control with two actual emitted same-fact blocks but one ledger row; the detector must fail it.

The real-PG session-epoch-cross-port.integration.test.ts exercises actual returned blocks and post-compaction re-prime. Delivery-assessment fixtures additionally discriminate concurrent/retry evidence; they are NOT an actual concurrent live-client drill. Report that applicability gap until exercised.

Epoch rows persist until the ledger age sweep (currently 14 days; re-read the writer before depending on retention). Inspect actual emitted blocks during a drill, with ledger rows used only for identity/epoch corroboration.

## Live end-to-end drill

First select the current-build route with dev:pipeline_position(path, testClass:'operator-api') and verify the served code. Use an isolated fixture scope; record source IDs, session ID, epoch, exact emitted blocks, relevant contracts and observation times. Plant two scoped fixture memories, then run one subject through: (A) fixture fact at session start, naming the delivery source; (B) compaction while holding the work item, with a focus that excludes carrying fixture values; (C) second fact post-compaction, naming its source. Actual prompt records establish delivery; independently checked task/completion evidence establishes consumption. Ledger stamps alone establish neither.

Historical protocol: recall-drill-2-injection-2026-07-12, EI-10406/EI-10407. Clean up fixture memories and the drill subject. Do not revive a retired emitter or schedule recurring paid judging merely because a historical card is old.

## Verification and truthful ratings

```bash
PAPERCUSP_TEST_RUN_HARNESS=papercusp npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/memory/recall-admission.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/memory/session-epoch-cross-port.integration.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/memory/corpus-recall.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/memory/injection-delivery-coverage.test.ts
```

Use scorecards:evaluate for the exact current skeleton, supply every criterion with population/window/runtime/evidence references, validate, then emit and inspect the saved card and freshness/trend. Distinguish manual/self-reported evidence from a registered platform-computed instrument. Healthy requires current valid evidence meeting the frozen policy; confirmed hard correctness failures are broken; insufficient measurements are unknown with a concrete next evidence action.
